questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience a city and country that I knew very little about. Also it was important for me to choose a very big city so there would be plenty to explore in my free-time! Also, my host university had a lot of interesting and relevant courses to choose from.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad experience went far over my own expectations. It was an amazing semester and all the hard work before the stay was worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: At times, it was a bit confusing to navigate between all the different sources (KU-net, UCPH abroad, Host university and their coordinators). But it was never more confusing than just sending an email with questions to either my coordinator at my home or host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival, all exchange students were invited to a welcoming orientation where courses, maps, social programmes etc. were explained. Further communication with the coordinator at SNU (Office of International Affairs (OIA)) was through informational e-mails. The coordinator responded very quickly to e-mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I didnt want to stay on campus, because SNU is kind of far from other parts of the city, that I would rather be close to. So I had to look for housing by my self and it was a very stressful proces. I wanted to get started early on finding housing, so I started several months before my scheduled departure, but I ended up not finding anything before a few weeks after my arrival. I looked at airbnb and kept my eyes on the different Facebook-groups (there are several groups on facebook for international exchange students looking for housing in Seoul!) and also though Google, I found a few options. I ended up finding a nice one-room, but a bit expensive. So - it was a very stressful process finding housing on my own, but that said - it all worked out in the end! Also, I was a bit picky, both on area, price and type of housing -  if you tone your expectations a bit down on these aspects, it will definitely be much easier to find housing! Some of my friends also stayed in Goshiwons near the campus - they were cheap and very nice also! You can look for goshiwons on
https://goshipages.com/
. Many of my friends stayed in the dorms and were totally happy with it! There are a few sharehouse communities as well: Check out Kims Community House, Avengers House and Simple Spaces.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a stressful and time-consuming proces, finding housing on your own off campus. But in my experience, I ended up finding a good match and staying near Sinchon/Hongdae which was really nice areas to be close to! So I think the work was worth it. Also - I ended up spending quite a lot of time on transportation (around 50 minutes each way). But I only had to be on campus 3/5 days, so that was okay for me. If I had more courses, I think it would have been a bit annoying to spend all that time on transportation. So - it definitely depends on your priorities, whether you should decide to live on or off campus!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: During the registration process, we were sent a couple of very long emails with a lot of information. At times it was a little bit tough to navigate in all the information and deadlines. Remember to check your email and read the emails really carefully so you dont miss any information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After nomination, you will receive an email from Office of International Affairs where they explain the further process. Then you will need to apply officially, submitting a list of documents (bank statement, letter of approval, list of passed subjects (with stamps), statement of purpose, a photo and passport scan). A couple of months after, you will receive the official letter of approval from SNU and then you can apply for the visa at the embassy in Denmark.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to ask questions through email to the OIA coordinator and she answered very quickly always!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. The course registration was a bit confusing to understand at first. It is split up in different tasks during 6 days. The first couple of days are "course cart shopping" and then it moves on to first-come-first-served. After that you can sign up for the courses that are not full. If you didnt get the course you wanted, you can send an application to the professor teaching the course, and they will decide if there is room for you as well. OIA has a youtube channel where they explain the course registration process! Check that out a few days before at least, to be sure that you know what is going down. Because some courses are really popular and will "sell out" in a matter of seconds. Luckily my classes werent as popular, but some of my friends didnt get all the courses they wanted during the first registration and had to ask the professor to get a spot. I will recommend that you make a prioritized list of the courses you want and plan out exactly which ones to apply to first. During the "course-cart-shopping"-days you can also get a hint of how popular the course is - for example if there are 25 spots and 80 people signed up, then you should try to get that course as the first thing you do, when the registration opens!:) And think of a plan-B as well!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of information at once. Dont stress about it - just notice the deadlines and read the emails carefully and maybe several times!:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the academic level were a bit lower than at univ. of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses are taught very differently from my experiences at Univ. of Copenhagen. There is a lot of focus on tests during the semester and memorizing terms. The work-load was similar to my home univ. but sometimes felt heavier, because on the focus on tests in stead of the final exam, as I know it from back home. So in my experience the semester was quite busy but not as busy closer to end of semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Globalizing Korea (Dep. of Anthropology)
Korean Language and Literature (Liberal studies)
Korean Musical Culture (Liberal Studies)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the courses I was enrolled in were really exciting and taught me a lot about different aspects of Korean Culture and I recommend all the courses. If you can, I will definitely recommend taking a course with Professor Charles La Shure, if you can. He was an excellent professor - very humorous and good at making a great teaching environment for the class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Flight tickets were really expensive. Restaurants are cheap but cooking yourself can be pretty expensive if your are not careful! Some grocery stores are cheaper than others and some "western" products can be really expensive as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a buddy-program at SNU you can sign up for and I will recommend every exchange student coming to SNU to sign up for it! It was absolutely wonderful and the korean buddies were super engaged! There is weekly dinners and events during the semester that you can sign up for. It was through the buddy program that I found my friends that I ended up spending a lot of time with and going traveling with as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: At the beginning of the semester, there is a club-festival, where all the clubs at campus will sit in a tent and play games, talk to other students or present what they do in that particular club. I will recommend that you go to this festival to check out which clubs are possible to sign up for - some of them dont accept exchange students that only are at SNU for one semester so ask about that as well! I initially signed up for the hiking-club but ended up not going to any of the trips because of lack of time! But they seemed really nice and active in that club:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much around the country as you possibly can! It is really easy and accessible to get around and the country has so many beautiful and interesting places to visit on the weekend or on day trips. If you like hiking, there are sooo many beautiful hikes around Seoul - even at campus:')

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy to adjust to the everyday-life in Seoul! The hardest thing for me was figuring out how to adjust my food habits, shopping in grocery stores and the restaurant culture. I am a vegetarian and meat is a big part of the Korean cuisine, so that was a bit challenging at times! But most restaurants have at least one vegetarian option, so it always worked out.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for the buddy program or the clubs at campus!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No talking in public transportation!:) Its always really quiet in public transportation and people will definitely give you the side-eye if you talk loudly with your friends!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The restaurant-culture is really cool! People usually eat out a lot to socialize with their friends or collegues and it was really fun, experiencing that part of korean culture, both with my international and korean friends! Also, people are extremely helpful if you ask for directions or help to transportation, so dont hesitate to ask if you are confused!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Get started with planning, getting the documents for the applications, searching for housing and saving up as soon as you possibly can! Some of the documents can take some time to get. 
2) Check your email often and read the emails from OIA several times so you dont miss any deadlines. 
3) Sign up for the buddy-program! It is really the best way of meeting people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Dont be afraid to reach out to your peer exchange students for help! In stead of spending hours on searching for the answer to your question on your own, another exchange student might just have been through the same frustrating process just before you! It could save you a lot of time. 
And this is more a recommendation for Korea in general: But get started on learning reading and writing hangul, before you go. It is very accessible and quick to learn and it has helped me out A LOT in being able to navigate in course material, traveling around the country and just in life in general in Seoul! Duolingo was perfectly enough but there are plenty of other accessible resources - like "Talk to me in Korean".

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over the world through the Buddy-program! I cannot stress enough how much I recommend signing up for that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The months before the exchange were actually more difficult and challenging for me than the actual exchange. The application process, searching for housing and all the other things you have to get in order before departure, were extremely stressful! BUT in the end, it all worked out and once I got there, all the work was 10 times worth it. There really is a lot of things to fix when you go on exchange and it can feel like an overload of information at some times. But just do it bit by bit and once it is all done, you can enjoy your semester and focus on your studies!:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
